questions.question: Why put tool execution in one dispatcher instead of in each tool?
options: Every tool then gets the same handling for unknown names, bad arguments, timeouts and errors
questions.explanation: One code path means consistent behaviour and one place to fix bugs.

questions.question: Why does the registry reject a second tool with the same name?
options: A silent overwrite would send calls to the wrong function
questions.explanation: Duplicate names are a bug that only shows up as wrong behaviour.

questions.question: A thread-pool timeout fires. What happens to the tool's thread?
options: It keeps running in the background; the dispatcher just stops waiting
questions.explanation: Threads can't be killed in Python. Use a subprocess when a tool must really stop.

questions.question: Why do hooks run after validation but before execution?
options: Permission checks see clean arguments, and a denied call never runs
questions.explanation: send_email to an outside address was blocked before anything was sent.

questions.question: Live, strict validation rejected 4 of 6 calls. What were the errors?
options: Numbers sent as strings and null for an optional parameter
questions.explanation: The values were right; only the types were off.

questions.question: Which coercion is NOT safe?
options: null on an optional parameter -> use the default
questions.explanation: Interpreting words is a guess. Reject it with a clear message instead.
